clue.text: Bill Clinton's first turn — worth being faithful?

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word Clinton's

parts.note: U, as in a U-turn
worth means rate, as in the rate of something

explanation.surface: A question about whether Bill Clinton's opening move was worthwhile for loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous name is a distraction: 'Bill' is AC, and only Clinton's first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful copy or account is one that is exact, true to the original.

clue.text: Law book

definitions.meaning: The English actor, so his first name goes with Law
the Epistle of ... is a short book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A legal textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense names the actor whose surname is Law; the other is a New Testament epistle.

clue.text: Do swim at sea to have the experience

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Swimming in the ocean gives you the experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the letters of DO SWIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is the knowledge and judgement gained through experience, so the two stand for each other loosely.

clue.text: Rehabilitate policemen giving up cocaine for dessert

indicators.note: to rehabilitate is to remake or reform, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order
giving up means dropping something, here a letter from the word policemen

parts.note: C is a slang abbreviation for cocaine

explanation.surface: Drug-using police officers are reformed by quitting cocaine in favour of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' drops the C of POLICEMEN, leaving POLIEMEN; 'Rehabilitate' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon pie, such as lemon meringue, is a sweet course served after a meal.

clue.text: Boxing chaps turn to a dramatic series of bouts

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one set of letters goes around the other
dramatic suggests a sensational upheaval, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Male boxers turn to a theatrical run of fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dramatic' rearranges TURN TO A into TOURNAT, which 'Boxing' wraps round MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a competition made up of a sequence of contests or matches.

clue.text: First goal accepted by 2 special referees

indicators.note: being accepted by means being taken in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer to 2 down, the New Testament book

indicators.note: First takes the opening letter of the word goal

explanation.surface: Officials allowing the opening goal, with a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The '2' points to the answer at 2 down, whose letters are split to take in the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges and referees are both officials who decide outcomes in contests or disputes.

clue.text: Busy trophy wife regularly featured in love record …

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: featured in means placed inside, so the next pieces go within the record

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
a cup is a trophy

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word wife

explanation.surface: A busy trophy wife keeps appearing on a romantic record, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'wife', I and E. The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupied means engaged or tied up, which is what being busy is.

clue.text: Diamonds with income support? — Home Secretary's alarm

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds
IS is short for Income Support, a UK state benefit
Theresa May was the UK Home Secretary when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A politician alarmed by jewels being paid for with welfare benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: Income Support is a British state benefit for people on low incomes; Theresa May was Home Secretary 2010-16.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a feeling of alarm and distress, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: … leaving former partner nothing — dirt, for the most part

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped from the word for dirt

parts.note: dust is dirt

explanation.surface: Walking out on an ex with nothing but grime, following on from the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts DUST to DUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, a great going-away; it is also the second book of the Bible.

clue.text: Boy's chance to go topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a fluke is a lucky chance

explanation.surface: A lad gets an opportunity to strip off his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' removes the first letter of FLUKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke is a common male first name, standing for any lad; it is also a Gospel book.

clue.text: I clean silver in Germany and pour on cold water

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the letters for the country

parts.note: DE is the international code for Germany (Deutschland)
to scour is to clean by scrubbing
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone polishes silverware in Germany and is dismissive of the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clean silver' reads as one household chore, but it splits into two pieces; Germany's code comes from Deutschland.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour cold water on an idea is an idiom for dampening enthusiasm, deterring someone.

clue.text: Uncontrolled actor ignores book on The Origin of Method

indicators.note: ignores means leaves out, so a letter is dropped from the actor's name

parts.note: Marlon Brando, the famous Method actor

indicators.note: The Origin of takes the opening letter of the word Method

explanation.surface: An actor skips reading Darwin-like book about the beginnings of Method acting.
explanation.walkthrough: Brando was the best-known Method actor, which makes the surface plausible; dropping B leaves RANDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means haphazard, without aim or control.

clue.text: Perhaps chocolate's the cause of universal expansion?

definitions.text: Perhaps chocolate's the cause of universal expansion?

parts.words: Perhaps chocolate's the cause of universal expansion?
parts.note: cosmologists blame an unseen force for the universe speeding apart; the surface suggests the bitter kind of chocolate makes everyone fat

explanation.surface: Is chocolate why everyone is getting bigger?
explanation.walkthrough: Read one way, the fuel in a bitter bar of chocolate; read the other, the physicists' name for what drives cosmic expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: In cosmology it is the hypothetical force accelerating the expansion of the universe.

clue.text: Review article is in abstract paper

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
abstract can mean removed or extracted, here signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A review piece appears in an academic paper's summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstract' looks like the summary of a paper but signals the anagram, giving PPRAE; 'in' then sets IS within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess or evaluate, which is what a review does.

clue.text: Man makes tea for Israelites

parts.note: HE is the male pronoun, a man
one brews tea

explanation.surface: A fellow puts the kettle on for the people of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebrews is another name for the ancient Israelites; it is also a New Testament epistle.

clue.text: Social workers sabotaged stand supporting film director

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting underneath, so this part comes after the director

parts.note: John Woo, the Hong Kong director of action films

indicators.note: sabotaged means wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Welfare staff wreck a set built for a film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sabotaged' rearranges STAND into DANTS. 'Social workers' are not caseworkers: ants are social insects and workers are the non-breeding caste.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood ants live in large colonies, and most of them are sterile worker ants.

clue.text: Seeing explosion — small or big bang?

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Watching a blast and wondering whether it was minor or huge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' scrambles the first word into GENESI; 'big bang?' is the definition, the question mark admitting it is an example of a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang is the origin of the universe, and genesis means origin or creation; it is also the Bible's first book.

clue.text: Mark breaks sonic barrier, emitting dreadful roar!

indicators.note: breaks means smashes up, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged
emitting means giving out, so the letters of the word roar, in any order, leave the mix

explanation.surface: A jet breaks the sound barrier with a terrible bellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SONIC BARRIER, remove the letters of ROAR (in a jumbled order, as 'dreadful' says), and rearrange what remains, SNICBRIE, as 'breaks' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to mark letters or words on a surface by writing or engraving.

clue.text: 1960s' model rejects fashion of bright pink

indicators.note: rejects means throws out, so a word is removed from the model's name

parts.note: Jean Shrimpton was a famous British model of the 1960s
ton is an old word for fashion or style

explanation.surface: A sixties model turns down a fashion for vivid pink.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Shrimpton was a leading British model of the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is the name of a bright pink colour, after the cooked shellfish.

clue.text: Is he an insect or a great beast?

parts.note: is is a form of the verb to be
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: Is that man a bug or a monster?
explanation.definitionFit: The Behemoth is a huge creature in the Book of Job, now any enormous animal.

clue.text: Enigmatist's debut puzzle divided Heaven and Hell

indicators.note: debut means first appearance, so the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle

explanation.surface: A setter's first crossword split opinion between delight and torment.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus was the dark region passed through between the living world and Hades.

clue.text: Copper's exam brings forth the cleverest

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A police officer's examination reveals the brightest candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean clever or shrewd, so the cutest is the shrewdest.

clue.text: It's rumoured minister could get fired

indicators.note: it's rumoured means people are saying it, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a canon is a member of the clergy, a minister

explanation.surface: Gossip says a clergyman could be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' looks like dismissed from a job; it is a gun being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large gun, something that can be fired.

clue.text: Twist a handle in to animate display

indicators.note: twist means turn round, so the words a and handle are read backwards

parts.note: a lever is a handle

indicators.note: animate means set in motion, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Turning a handle brings a show to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' turns A LEVER into REVELA; 'animate' rearranges IN TO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is a disclosure, something shown or laid open; it is also the last book of the Bible.

clue.text: Yank's clothing slips off hip

indicators.note: slips off means is removed, so a piece is taken off the garment

parts.note: a jerkin is a sleeveless jacket
in means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: An American's garment slides off his hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American; it is a sharp pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerk is a sudden sharp pull, the same as a yank.

clue.text: Sign card about American singer-songwriter

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the star sign and the card together are read backwards

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
J is the jack, a playing card

explanation.surface: Signing a card for an American musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Joel is an American singer-songwriter; Joel is also an Old Testament prophet's book.

clue.text: Economical plan

definitions.meaning: cheap, low-cost, as in a cut-price airline

explanation.surface: A thrifty scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means inexpensive; as a noun it is a spending plan.

clue.text: Words of 3 for doing words

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
verbs are known as doing words

explanation.surface: Wise sayings in favour of action words.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer at 3 down, so the definition is 'words of wisdom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs are short sayings of practical wisdom; it is also the Old Testament book of them.
